title: Role briefs: explicit acceptance criteria for every role and every resumed round
lead: *Proposed.* Every role brief ends its instructions with a `## Done when` checklist: what this role must have produced to be finished, the exact report lines, the commands its sandbox allows, and what to write when a check cannot run. The text is specific to the role, to the round (first, fix round, resumed) and to the finish step. The slice's own `Failing tests` and `Check` items are named in it, not left for the role to find.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-03: when ork instructs a role it should be explicit, above all about acceptance criteria for what that role is doing; ork is the orchestrator, so this matters more for ork than for any one session. Fact: rg for "acceptance" and "done when" in internal/roles/prompts/*.md finds nothing. Evidence of the gap (wave 7): the Claude fallback wrote "## 7. Owner needed" and a Tests: line with trailing text, and one implementer ended with Tests: 0 passed after the sandbox denied python3.12, because the brief did not say what a finished round must show or what to do when a check cannot run. Needed: each role brief (implementer, reviewer, gate, architect, spec-check, UI pass, and the Resumed session section) states, as a short checklist, what the role must have produced to be done: the exact report lines and headings, the test command that works in its sandbox, and what to write when a check is blocked. Related: S276 (the two report lines), S275, S256.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner 2026-11-03: when ork instructs a role it should be explicit, above all about acceptance criteria for what that role is doing. ork is the orchestrator, so this matters more for ork than for any one session. Fact at HEAD of main (read 2026-11-04): a search for "acceptance", "done when" and "done-criteria" in `internal/roles/prompts/*.md` and `internal/engine/brief.go` finds nothing. The brief (`BuildBrief`, `internal/engine/brief.go:60-155`) holds the prompt, the slice JSON, the tracking rule, the workspace limit, the environment, the files, the checks ork runs and the owner's sections; none says what a finished round must show.

Evidence from wave 7 (2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04):

- Claude fallback implementers (sonnet, haiku) wrote `## 4. Tests` and `## 7. Owner needed`, and a Tests line with trailing text. Five runs paused (S275, S276).
- An implementer ended with `Tests: 0 passed` after its sandbox denied `python3.12`. The brief never said what to write when a check cannot run, so the run recorded a false zero.
- The slicer implementers were denied `python3 -m unittest ...` with a pipe or an env prefix, and `slicer note` and `handoff` in the finish step. They did not know which exact forms their allowlist accepts (the allowlist is `DefaultImplementerAllowlist`, `internal/engine/perm.go:23-35`, or the project's registry entry). The s313 reviewer then raised a `[fix]` for tracking steps the implementer could not run (owner note 2026-11-04), costing a fix round.
- A resumed implementer (S275, round 2) again ended without a Tests line.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/engine/brief_test.go`, beside `TestBriefNamesCheckCommand` (line 141):

- `TestEveryRoleBriefHasADoneWhenSection`: all six roles have a `## Done when` section with at least three checklist lines and fewer than 40 lines. Fails first: no section.
- `TestImplementerDoneWhenNamesTheExactReportLines`: literal `Tests: N passed, M failed` and `## Owner needed`, nothing after counts, skipped tests under item 6, report order and docs. Fails first: no section.
- `TestImplementerDoneWhenListsTheSlicesFailingTestsAndChecks`: slice JSON names TestA and TestB, each red before the code, green after, and two exact check commands; excludes HUMAN CHECK items and states the slice lists none for missing sections. Fails first: no section.
- `TestImplementerDoneWhenShowsTheAllowedCommands`: default Allow entries plus a configured check command are printed verbatim, other commands are denied, no pipes/cd/env prefix unless allowed; ReadOnly says may only read. Fails first: no section.
- `TestDoneWhenSaysWhatToWriteWhenACheckCannotRun`: denied or impossible checks under item 6 with verbatim command and denial, actual test counts, never a made-up zero, ork re-runs outside the sandbox. Fails first: no section.
- `TestFixRoundDoneWhenListsEachFinding`: two [fix] findings each have their own proving-test or stated-no-test-reason line in Review findings, Gate FAIL, and Architect findings; no [later] work included. Fails first: no section.
- `TestResumedBriefRepeatsDoneWhen`: section after Resumed session, first re-run git status and git diff. Fails first: no section.
- `TestFinishStepDoneWhen`: ordered closing note and finish commands; denied finish command under Owner needed for orchestrator, engine.denials, no retry and no Tests requirement. Fails first: no section.
- `TestReviewerAndGateDoneWhen`: file:line plus reproduction/test for fixes, later scores, read-only and Owner needed; denied tracking is untagged reviewer (C) commentary or gate Deviation for the orchestrator evidence, never a fix; gate exact verdict first line, evidence per criterion, Tests line and verdict rule. Fails first: no section.

In `internal/roles/roles_test.go`:

- `TestPromptsPointAtDoneWhen`: every prompt points at the brief Done when section and says it overrides nothing in the report parts. Fails first: none does.

- `TestDoneWhenSeparatesBulletsAcrossProse` in `internal/engine/brief_test.go:477`: Failing tests and Check bullets retain indented continuations, exclude unindented prose and detached indented prose, and preserve the next bullet. Fails first: unindented prose contaminates the preceding item.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first from the failing list; confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. Add a `doneWhen(in BriefInput) string` function in `brief.go` that builds the checklist from fixed per-role text plus the slice's own sections (parse `Failing tests` and `Check` from `SliceJSON`; if a section is missing, say "the slice lists none" and do not invent items). Items are `- [ ] ...` lines; keep the whole section under 40 lines.
3. Implementer, first round: every failing test red before the product code and green after; the Check commands that are not HUMAN CHECK items run or reported blocked; docs updated in the same diff; the report in the order of the prompt; the two literal lines; the allowed command forms (print `Allow` as given: no pipes, no `cd`, no env prefix unless an entry allows it); what to do when blocked. Fix round: one line per `[fix]` finding. Resumed round: first re-run `git status` and the diff (S256), then the same checklist. Finish step: the finish commands in order; a denied one is not retried.
4. Reviewer and gate: the read-only fact, the report lines each must end with, `[fix]` needs `file:line` plus a reproduction or test, `[later]` needs scores, a tracking step the implementer was denied is a Deviation. Gate: first line, evidence per criterion, Tests line, verdict rule.
5. Architect, UI pass, spec check: the lines each report ends with (`## Owner needed`; the spec check writes "none" there), read-only fact, what counts as a finding.
6. Do not duplicate the report parts list from the prompts; the checklist refers to them by item number and adds only the criteria. Do not change the shape check or the parser.
7. Update `docs/design.md` and `docs/state.md` in the same diff.

Owner decisions (2026-11-05): Where does a reviewer or gate write a tracking step the implementer was denied? -> Commentary line: one untagged line under section (C) for the reviewer. The gate gets one "Deviation for the orchestrator" evidence line beside its criterion lines. Neither is a finding, so neither starts a fix round. [roles.denied-tracking-step].

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/engine ./internal/roles -run 'DoneWhen|TestPromptsPointAtDoneWhen|FirstRowBrief|BriefNamesCheckCommand'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- `rg -n "Done when" internal/engine/brief.go` shows the section built once; `rg -n "Done when" internal/roles/prompts` lists all six prompts.
- Mutation: build `doneWhen` without the `Allow` list; `TestImplementerDoneWhenShowsTheAllowedCommands` goes red. Drop the per-finding lines; `TestFixRoundDoneWhenListsEachFinding` goes red.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Read one real implementer brief from a running slice (`ork show` once S281 lands, or the role's prompt in the vendor log): the `## Done when` section names that slice's failing tests and the command forms its sandbox allows.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Role briefs end with a Done when checklist".
